key_insight: A melody-aware curriculum masking schedule for single-encoder masked modeling substantially strengthens cross-attention between melody and harmony, yielding more faithful and better-generalizing harmonizations—especially on out-of-domain melodies.
problem_solved: Existing masked-sequence training curricula (inspired by discrete diffusion) produce weak cross-attention between melody and harmony, so models underutilize melodic cues and fail to generalize to novel or out-of-domain melodies.
method: Frame harmonization as masked sequence modeling with a single encoder transformer that processes interleaved melody and harmony tokens.

Introduce melody-aware curriculum masking schedules that control which tokens are masked over training (e.g., melody-first / harmony-first / progressive difficulty) to encourage stronger cross-attention to the melody.
Diagnose cross-attention patterns and evaluate improvements with objective metrics and subjective listening tests, including out-of-domain generalization checks.
impact: Provides a simple, training-time recipe to make single-encoder generative music models pay more attention to lead melodies, improving harmony quality and robustness—an approach applicable to other masked-sequence tasks where cross-conditioned signals matter.
visual_elements: Schematic of the single-encoder input (interleaved melody+harmony) with attention flow arrows to illustrate cross-attention.
Curriculum timeline plot showing masking schedule changes over training (mask ratios for melody vs. harmony across epochs).
Before/after attention heatmaps comparing cross-attention strength and localization.
Bar chart (or paired violin plots) showing objective/subjective quality gains and out-of-domain performance improvements.
paper_title: Pay (Cross) Attention to the Melody: Curriculum Masking for Single-Encoder Melodic Harmonization
paper_authors: Maximos Kaliakatsos-Papakostas, Dimos Makris, Konstantinos Soiledis, Konstantinos-Theodoros Tsamis, Vassilis Katsouros
